newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF to ease regulations on bank branches.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF to ease regulations on bank branches.

text.p: Japan's Finance Ministry (MOF) said on Monday it would ease regulations that prevent banks from establishing domestic branches wherever they please, as well as rules on branch business hours.
MOF plans to ease the regulations as soon as possible, probably in June or July, although a firm time schedule has not yet been decided, a ministry official said.
Last March, Japan announced a package of broad measures to deregulate the nation's economy, which included relaxing regulations on banks' regional branches.
Currently, Japanese banks cannot open branch offices wherever they wish because of MOF regulations which try to avoid the concentration of banks in one area.
Banks must also report branch business hours to the Finance Ministry.
The MOF official said banks will be able to provide better services if such regulations were abolished.
Some Japanese banks may start offering 24-hour banking services, a practice not seen in Japan, although common in some Western countries, he said.
High costs have deterred Japanese banks from operating 24 hours a day.
However, banks are expected to start offering 24-hour banking services as competition grows in the wake of the nation's financial deregulation, banking industry sources said.
